latest_release.name: Coucou 0.5.8
latest_release.body:
Coucou 0.5.8 for macOS 15 or later (Apple silicon and Intel).

Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

## What's new

Fixes by @Ohualtex.

- **Approval comes back after a question** — answering a question now brings back the approval that was waiting behind it (#993 by @Ohualtex, #851)
- **Questions stay put** — a new permission request or switching pills no longer sends a waiting question back to the terminal; opening the island shows it again (#994 by @Ohualtex, #852)
- **Desktop Mochi stays visible** — Mochi no longer disappears from the desktop when you switch apps (#992 by @Ohualtex, #921)
- **Dropped files no longer overwrite each other** — a second file with the same name is kept beside the first, and the copies Coucou keeps are cleaned up after 7 days (#986 by @Ohualtex, #856)
- **No misplaced Writing Tools button** — the island's text fields no longer show the macOS Writing Tools button near the notch (#997 by @Ohualtex, #936)

## Install

1. Download Coucou.zip below and unzip it.
2. Move Coucou.app to your Applications folder, replacing the old one if you have it.
3. Launch it, and click Open when macOS asks you to confirm.

Linux and Windows: see the [README](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou#readme).

detail.readme_excerpt:
# Coucou **A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows and Linux — and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. And now on your phone too: iPhone and Android.** Approve permissions, watch your agents work, drop a file, chat with Claude — all without leaving what you're doing. Walk away from your Mac and Mochi follows you to your iPhone: Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, widgets, Siri. **New in 0.4: Coucou is a real Mac app.** Hold a key anywhere, speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, like Wispr Flow — free, open source, and offline with Parakeet. Record your calls without a bot in the meeting and get the transcript, the summary and the to-dos. [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Louis-CFM/coucou?filter=v*&label=version&color=0A84FF)](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou/releases) ![macOS 15+](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-15%2B-black?logo=apple) ![iOS 18+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-18%2B-black?logo=apple) ![Android 11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-11%2B-3DDC84?logo=android&logoColor=white) ![Windows 10/11](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11-0078D4?logo=windows&logoColor=white) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-AppImage%20%7C%20deb%20%7C%20rpm-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![Swift 6](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-6-F05138?logo=swift&logoColor=white) ![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/SwiftUI-native-0A84FF) ![Tauri 2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tauri-2-FFC131?logo=tauri&logoColor=black) ![Code: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-MIT-green) ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Louis-CFM/coucou?style=social)
--- ## Why Some studios showed off gorgeous notch companions… and never let anyone use them. **Coucou is the open version.** Every line of code is open source under the MIT License: read it, fork it, learn from it. The Coucou name, Mochi and the sounds stay © Louis Raillé (see [License](#license)).
